title: Customer-impact-first routing framework for hosted chat streams with tool/function calls
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Incoming enterprise feature requests for hosted chat streaming with tool/function calling and structured outputs are high volume and varied quality. Current intake funnels prioritize raw signal counts and manual review, causing slow SLAs for high-impact customers and inconsistent routing between Hosted/Dedicated/Private offerings.

Goal: Define an automated, tenant-adaptive routing and prioritization framework that ranks inbound feature requests by customer impact and operational risk, then routes them to the appropriate intake lane (self-serve backlog, PM review, fast-track enterprise onboarding). The framework should: 1) surface high-business-impact asks quickly, 2) enforce SLOs for enterprise SLA customers, 3) integrate with existing Hosted API eligibility gates and console product tiers, and 4) be auditable for compliance.

Success metrics (targeted): median time-to-triage for high-impact customers <= 3 business days, % of enterprise-eligible requests auto-classified >= 65%, reduction in manual triage time for PM team by 35%, and first-response NPS on intake <= 7 days for priority lanes.

Scope: inbound non-bug product requests involving chat streaming, multi-tool/function calling sequences, or requests for structured outputs/format contracts. Out of scope: infra-only capacity requests, bugs, or small SDK/Docs asks.

Proposed approach: 1) Build a weighted scoring model combining tenant signals (commit level, monthly spend, SLA tier), request-level signals (estimated QPS, data sensitivity, multi-turn complexity, required tool integrations), and behavioral signals (request history, prior escalations). 2) Implement routing policies: auto-eligible enterprise lane, PM review queue, self-serve backlog. 3) Add immediate guardrails that escalate requests that mention high-risk terms (PII, regulated data, HIPS) to security review. 4) Expose a minimal customer-facing eligibility response explaining why a request was routed. 5) Instrument observability: per-lane throughput, time-to-triage, false-positive rate, and manual override counts.

Acceptance criteria: documented scoring rubric in Confluence, P0/P1/P2 mapping to intake lanes, a working prototype classifier integrated with intake form (alpha), automated notification flows to PM and Solutions for enterprise-eligible requests, and dashboarding in Metrics (Grafana) showing the success metrics above.

Risks & trade-offs: heavy automation risks misclassifying nuanced requests — initial rollout will default to conservative thresholds and include human-in-the-loop checks. Data sensitivity labeling requires Security buy-in and may increase manual work initially. The scoring model needs calibration to avoid bias toward large-spend tenants that could drown smaller strategic accounts; include a manual appeal path.

Related artifacts: PRD draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Customer+Impact+Routing+Framework (internal), intake form prototype: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abc-example (internal), initial classifier notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pm-intake-classifier/pulls/14 (PR), dashboard mock: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd-intake-routing (internal).
